sections.content: Native CSS nesting lets you write child rules inside parents — like preprocessors but built into browsers now. & refers to the parent selector.
.card { .title { } &:hover { } } compiles conceptually to .card .title and .card:hover. Specificity of & matches the parent.
Key points: nesting is widely supported now, keep it shallow (2 levels), and & is required when the nested selector doesn't start with a combinator-friendly pattern.
